title: First Upload + Final Assessment
summary: Walk through your first upload and pass the final lesson quiz.

steps.title: First Upload Walkthrough
steps.markdownContent:
Time to put it all together and upload your first sketch! We will use the built-in Blink example.

1. **Connect**: Plug the Arduino into USB.
2. **Open Sketch**: In the IDE, go to File > Examples > 01.Basics > Blink.
3. **Select Board**: Tools > Board > Arduino Uno.
4. **Select Port**: Tools > Port > [Select your port].
5. **Verify**: Click the Checkmark button to compile.
6. **Upload**: Click the Right Arrow button to flash.
7. **Observe**: Look at the board. The built-in LED near pin 13 should blink on and off every second!

quickCheck.question: When uploading a sketch, what indicator lights on the Arduino Uno flash to show data is transferring?
options: The TX and RX LEDs flash rapidly
quickCheck.explanation: The TX (Transmit) and RX (Receive) LEDs blink rapidly as code bytes stream over the USB cable!
quickCheck.warmupExplanation: Watch the TX and RX lights dance when your code travels into the board!

quickCheck.question: Congratulations! What have you mastered by completing Lesson 2B?
options: The entire Arduino IDE workflow: writing sketches, selecting boards/ports, compiling, and flashing hardware
Only how to click a mouse
quickCheck.explanation: You now know how to take ideas from your mind, turn them into code, and upload them to real hardware!
quickCheck.warmupExplanation: You are officially equipped with the master tools of an embedded software engineer!

steps.title: Common Failures
steps.markdownContent:
If the LED doesn't blink, review these common failures:
- **Upload Error (avrdude sync)**: You likely chose the wrong Port. Check the Tools > Port menu again.
- **Compilation Error**: You might have accidentally deleted a semicolon or curly brace `{` in the code.
- **No Lights At All**: The USB cable isn't pushed in fully, or the port is dead.

steps.title: Comprehensive Knowledge Check
steps.markdownContent: Verify your understanding of IDE compilation, USB device drivers, COM ports, and firmware lifecycles.

interactiveConfig.question: What does IDE stand for?
interactiveConfig.explanation: IDE stands for Integrated Development Environment—the unified coding and flashing workbench.

questions.question: What does IDE stand for?
questions.explanation: IDE stands for Integrated Development Environment—the unified coding and flashing workbench.

questions.question: What is an Arduino sketch?
questions.explanation: An Arduino sketch is the C++ program file containing setup() and loop() routines.

questions.question: What does compiling do?
options: Converts source code into a form suitable for the target system
questions.explanation: The compiler translates human-readable C++ source text into hexadecimal machine opcodes.

questions.question: What does Upload do?
options: Sends the program to the Arduino
questions.explanation: Upload uses the avrdude utility to transfer compiled hex binary through USB into microcontroller flash memory.

questions.question: Why must you select the correct board?
options: Different boards can use different hardware and programming requirements
The board name changes the USB cable
questions.explanation: Different microcontroller boards use distinct pin layouts, register maps, and flash sizes.

questions.question: What does the port identify?
options: The computer's communication connection to the Arduino
questions.explanation: The serial COM port provides the virtual UART communication link between host OS and the Uno board.

questions.question: What does Serial.begin() do?
options: Initializes serial communication to talk to the computer
questions.explanation: It prepares the hardware to send and receive text.

questions.question: What is the difference between setup() and loop()?
options: setup() runs once, loop() runs repeatedly forever
setup() is optional, loop() is not
setup() compiles code, loop() uploads it
questions.explanation: setup() initializes hardware once on boot. loop() cycles endlessly to process real-time events.
